subject.title: Feature: Auto session split when approaching context window limit

question: Should OpenClaw add a core context-pressure automatic session rollover policy, and what public config, default behavior, continuity payload, and delivery-safety contract should it use?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but implementing it defines new public session lifecycle behavior and can affect config compatibility, channel routing, stored session state, privacy, and provider/auth continuity.

options.title: Approve opt-in core rollover
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default core session policy with explicit token thresholds, durable handoff storage, delivery identity preservation, and focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Fold into broader lifecycle design
options.body: Keep this open but implement it together with age, turn-count, and context-pressure rotation so OpenClaw has one session lifecycle contract.

options.title: Defer automatic rollover
options.body: Document compaction, memoryFlush, truncateAfterCompaction, and manual reset as the supported mitigations until maintainers want a larger lifecycle surface.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in core rollover
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default core session policy with explicit token thresholds, durable handoff storage, delivery identity preservation, and focused upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across daily reset, memory flush, session config, and adjacent session lifecycle behavior.
